claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the exported function returns their unsigned greatest common divisor encoded as a 32-bit value.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: For every pair of unsigned 32-bit values, the statement returns their greatest common divisor; that value fits in 32 bits, so encoding it does not change it.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Both inputs range over every 32-bit bit pattern and are interpreted as unsigned natural numbers for the greatest-common-divisor calculation.
The result is the natural-number greatest common divisor encoded in 32 bits; encoding with a 32-bit bitvector wraps modulo 2³² if needed.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.

claims.summary: For every three 32-bit inputs, the exported function selects a value using signed comparisons against the two bounds and returns it.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The signed comparisons implement the stated lower-bound, upper-bound, otherwise-input rule for every input, including when the bounds are reversed.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: All three inputs range over every 32-bit bit pattern and are compared as signed 32-bit integers.
The function returns the lower bound if the input is signed-less than it; otherwise it returns the upper bound if the upper bound is signed-less than the input; otherwise it returns the input.
The selected input is returned unchanged, with no arithmetic or wraparound in the stated result.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The ordering is signed, but the claim ranges over all bit patterns, so values with the top bit set represent negative signed values for comparisons.
No requirement says the lower bound is less than or equal to the upper bound; the nested comparisons specify the result even when the bounds are reversed.
